overview: Black plays ...b6 and ...Bb7 against 2.Nf3, aiming for a hypermodern pressure on e4 and the long diagonal instead of the usual Sicilian set-ups. White typically takes the centre with 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Bb7 5.Nc3 and gets a comfortable game. Reading is from the moves; no subtree data was given.

white_ideas.idea: Open the position with d4 and play Nc3 and Bd3 with a space edge
Use the extra central space and the e4 pawn against the b7 bishop

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the queen's bishop and press on e4 and the long diagonal
Develop ...Nf6, ...e6 and ...Be7 with a flexible, solid structure

typical_structures.structure: Open Sicilian structure with Black bishop on b7 and a half-open c-file

character.notes: Quiet, hypermodern, with White having a small edge in space.

soundness.notes: Playable but considered slightly inferior to main Sicilians.

structure.notes: The Open Sicilian asymmetry with a half-open c-file.

level.notes: Needs understanding of the fianchetto structure but little theory.

character.reason: Quiet development with no clear risk on either side.

soundness.reason: Playable, if slightly inferior for Black.

structure.reason: An asymmetric Sicilian centre with a half-open c-file.

plans.reason: The b7 bishop on the long diagonal defines Black's play.
